title: SHAD Canada
cost: ~$2,400 CAD program fee (need-based financial aid and full bursaries available)
description: A month-long summer enrichment program hosted at Canadian universities where students tackle entrepreneurial STEM design challenges. Highly regarded by Canadian universities as a marker of academic excellence and initiative.

title: Pascal Contest
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A Waterloo math contest for Grade 9 students (and younger) that tests problem-solving beyond the regular curriculum. A good first step into the Waterloo contest sequence leading to Cayley, Fermat, and Euclid.

title: Cayley Contest
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A Waterloo math contest for Grade 10 students (and younger) that emphasizes creative problem solving. Strong results help students build toward the senior contests.

title: Fermat Contest
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A Waterloo math contest for Grade 11 students (and younger) with challenging, multi-step problems. Demonstrates quantitative reasoning for STEM and engineering applications.

title: Euclid Mathematics Contest
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A challenging math contest for senior students that is widely used by Waterloo and other universities for scholarship and admission consideration. Strong results demonstrate advanced problem-solving skills valued in engineering and math programs.

title: Galois Contest
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A full-solution Waterloo contest for Grade 10 students (and younger) where students write out complete, well-reasoned solutions. Builds mathematical communication skills.

title: Hypatia Contest
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A full-solution Waterloo contest for Grade 11 students (and younger) that rewards clear, complete written reasoning. A good step between Galois and Euclid.

title: Canadian Intermediate Mathematics Contest (CIMC)
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A Waterloo contest for intermediate students with curriculum-based and extension problems, written in the fall. Good preparation for the Fermat and Euclid contests.

title: Canadian Senior Mathematics Contest (CSMC)
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A national math contest testing curriculum-based problem solving for senior high school students, written in the fall. Participation and awards strengthen STEM applications and demonstrate quantitative reasoning ability.

title: Canadian Computing Competition (CCC)
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A programming contest with Junior and Senior divisions testing algorithmic problem-solving in any language, used by top computer science programs to identify talented applicants. Top scorers may qualify for the Canadian Computing Olympiad.

title: Canadian Computing Olympiad (CCO)
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: The national computer science olympiad for top performers on the Canadian Computing Competition. Results are used to select Canada's team for the International Olympiad in Informatics.

title: Canadian Team Mathematics Contest (CTMC)
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A team-based Waterloo math contest where students collaborate on problems, building teamwork alongside problem-solving skills.
